proves: FINDING (behavior resolution): with two actor types in one module declaring the same behavior name with different semantics, 'send s hit()' executes the FIRST declaration's code -- First.hit (+100) -- against Second's state (Second.hit would add 1). The compiler resolves behavior names by suffix match against the variable name (operand_name_hint returns the variable name, not its type), so 's.hit' falls back to the first '.hit' in the module behavior table. mir_lower.rs documents this as a known ambiguity inherited from the stable compiler; SPEC2 8.5's name-based dispatch does not mention it.
